Can anyone clarify this Chase 5/24 question? I know that Chase offers certain cards that are exempt from the 5/24 rule (e.g. Chase Hyatt card), meaning you are eligible for this card without regard to how many cards you’ve opened in the previous 24 months. Does that also mean that this card does not count against you in regard to 5/24 for any future applications to Chase for cards that are subject to 5/24?

No, certain business cards are the ONLY thing that will not count against 5/24. Chase tells whether you are 5/24 (mainly) by looking at your credit report. Nearly all cards are reported to your credit report.

You CAN get certain Chase cards even if you are over 5/24. (I believe Marriott and IHG are examples.)

Bank of America business cards are a real pain – I want to warn people about them. I know you don’t have them listed right now, but I wanted to make you aware. I have been trying to get the $200 promotional credit that I earned for several months. When you call, there’s always a 20-30 minute wait stated, although call-backs are available. I’ve had to wait over an hour for a call-back, even when they said it would be 20-30 minutes. B of America is trying to do everything they can to not provide customer service. They want you to provide the date you opened the card, your FULL social security number (providing this to a person increases your risk of identity theft), and answer a series of questions. I’ve called twice now about the promotion and both times, it was confirmed I had met the terms. The first time, I had just met the terms so I waited 2 months to call back. The second time, the person said they were putting in a request for me to get the promotion – that was a over a month ago. Still no promotion. I can’t imagine business owners are willing to put up with this. I’ll be taking my credit card business elsewhere.
